title: Oxidation Number Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
In a tug of war the stronger side pulls the rope its way, and in a game every player gets a score. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 7, Redox Reactions) Diya looks at a water molecule and asks who lost electrons when nobody gives them away fully.

You will see why shared electrons need a new bookkeeping idea, then score water on the molecule bench: each shared pair goes to the stronger puller, oxygen, so O is -2, each H is +1 and the total is 0. We define oxidation number, show that oxidation means the number goes up and reduction means it goes down, learn the rules (free element 0, ion = charge, sum = 0 or the ion charge) and the fixed scores (F -1, Group 1 +1, Group 2 +2, H +1 or -1 in metal hydrides, O -2 but -1 in peroxides, -1/2 in superoxides, positive with F), name compounds in Stock notation, compare oxygen in water and hydrogen peroxide, find chromium as +6 in K2Cr2O7, show the peroxide trap, then an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 72 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

In this video:
0:00 Who pulled the electrons?
0:30 The problem: shared electrons

2:26 Stock notation
2:46 Oxygen in water vs hydrogen peroxide
3:20 Worked example: Cr in K2Cr2O7
